Corpulent

KOR-pyuh-lunt · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Corpulent is fat; having a large, heavy body.

Centuries-old tavern records describe the innkeeper as a corpulent man famous for eating three full meals before noon.

Worked Example

The retired boxer had grown so corpulent since his championship days that old fans barely recognized him.

Corpulent specifically describes a large, heavy body -- it's a formal, almost clinical way to say 'fat.'

How Corpulent Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

portly

portly: somewhat fat, often used politely of an older man

stout

stout: solidly built and thickset, often heavy

Antonyms

gaunt

gaunt: so thin that bones are visible, often from illness

lean

lean: thin in a healthy, fit way

How Strong Is It? — plump → corpulent → obese

plump vs. corpulent

plump vs. corpulent: Plump means pleasantly rounded, only mildly overweight -- milder than corpulent.

obese vs. corpulent

obese vs. corpulent: Obese is a medical term for being dangerously overweight, an even stronger term than corpulent.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — corp-

Root — corp-: body (Latin corpus, 'body')

Suffix — -ulent

Suffix — -ulent: full of (Latin -ulentus)

Put it together

Put it together: Corpulent comes from Latin corpus ('body'): corp- ('body') + -ulent ('full of') -- literally 'full of body.'
